system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)

G2: production on-call

# OUTPUT 1: CV
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on CI/CD engineering, ephemeral
test-environment design and build tooling, and additional personal Kubernetes, GitOps and Terraform
infrastructure work. Experienced with GitLab CI, Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments,
and with improving pipeline speed, reliability and observability. Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s
cluster managed with GitOps and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure. Currently preparing for the
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam. Owns CI/CD and test-environment improvements for three
product teams, documents internal platform usage for onboarding, and enables QA and product teams to review
and test changes in isolated environments. Owns CI/CD and test-environment improvements for three product
teams, documents platform usage for onboarding, and mentors junior QA engineers.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure engineering and delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes
(namespace-level access), k3s, Argo CD, ephemeral environments, GitOps, observability
Infrastructure as Code: Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS infrastructure project)
Monitoring, networking and security: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik ingress, cert-manager, TLS
certificate management.
Programming and data: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, PostgreSQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems: Linux, Git, Ansible (basic)
Cloud learning: AWS free tier (EC2 and S3 basics); no professional cloud-platform experience
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw 2021–Present
• Own and improve GitLab CI/CD pipelines for three product teams ( 25 developers), covering build, unit,
integration and end-to-end test stages, plus artifact publishing.
• Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling workflows, parallelising test jobs, caching
dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs decreased by about
30%.
• Designed and operated merge-request ephemeral environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on a
shared Kubernetes cluster; each environment included the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, with
automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
• Enabled QA and product teams to review changes and run end-to-end tests in isolated environments before
merge.
• Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from
7% to below 1%.
• Built a Python and PostgreSQL pipeline-results collection workflow and Grafana dashboards to identify flaky
tests by team.
• Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data.
• Authored the internal guide to CI pipeline usage used in onboarding and mentored two QA interns in 2023.
QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw 2019–2021
• Tested web and mobile applications through manual and automated testing for client projects.
• Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
• Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.
Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House 2018–2019
• Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.
SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal 2024–2025
• Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster and deployed applications from a Git repository using Argo CD.
• Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring; configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS
certificate management in a personal k3s environment.
• Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used Ansible at a basic level.
Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health 2023
• Collected GitLab CI test results through the GitLab API into PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards
showing flaky tests by team; helped teams reduce the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
• Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.
EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology 2018
CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation | Exam scheduled for January 2027
LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility team,
I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. Over the
past seven years in QA engineering, I’ve increasingly focused on the infrastructure that helps
product teams build, test and deliver reliably. At Odrava Health, I own and improve GitLab CI/CD
pipelines and merge-request test environments for three product teams, helping make changes easier
to validate and safer to deliver.
I’ve reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about
30%, and helped bring the flaky-test rate in a suite of approximately 900 tests from 7% to below 1%.
I also designed short-lived environments deployed with Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster, with
seeded PostgreSQL data and automatic cleanup. I own these improvements for three product teams
of approximately 25 developers and enable QA and product colleagues to review changes and run
end-to-end tests before merge. This work involves making infrastructure usable for others and
documenting internal practices for onboarding.
Alongside my professional work, I built a three-node k3s homelab where applications are deployed
from Git using Argo CD. I set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki, configured Traefik and
cert-manager for TLS certificate management, and provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform.
I have also used the AWS free tier for basic EC2 and S3 learning exercises, although my professional
infrastructure experience has been primarily with GitLab CI, Kubernetes, and personal Hetzner
infrastructure. I’m currently preparing for the CKA exam. These projects have strengthened my
practical understanding of infrastructure automation, observability, Linux-based environments, and
TLS certificate management, while giving me a foundation to grow further in cloud infrastructure
engineering.
Corvale’s work connecting vehicle systems with cloud services is a compelling setting for this next
step. I’d bring hands-on experience improving delivery workflows, making shared infrastructure
usable for multiple teams, documenting technical practices for onboarding, and using measurable
analysis to improve reliability and cost. Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the
opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Fleet Connectivity team.
Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise
